messages:
Alex C: Heads-up: after the 12:05 deploy we saw a rare correctness regression in multi-tenant reads. tenant-B started getting responses for keys that had just been evicted by tenant-A's prefix purge. logs attached below.

Maria G: whoa. can you paste the repro logs?

Alex C: here's the short excerpt:
```
2026-05-18T12:05:14Z INFO evict: tenant=A prefix=/models/legacy/ id=0x7f6
2026-05-18T12:05:14Z DEBUG cache: remove_ptr ptr=0x55a3 stale=false
2026-05-18T12:05:14Z INFO read: tenant=B key=/models/legacy/123 ptr=0x55a3 hit=true
```

Alex C: note: ptr is the same address. we expect ptr to be invalid after eviction.

Jonathan: hmm, looks like a classic race where eviction clears residency but another shard still had a pointer in-flight. does our lease/ownership model guarantee single-writer?

Priyanka: currently eviction sets "resident=false" under eviction lock, then we publish an invalidation token asynchronously to other shards. there is a small window where read path checks residency without seeing the invalidation.

Sam K: so read path: load ptr -> check ptr->resident flag -> use. if invalidation hasn't propagated, you'll use a freed slab region. could be use-after-free or just stale data.

Maria G: any crashes? or just stale values returned?

Alex C: only stale values so far, no OOB crashes; likely memory freed/pinned by allocator for a bit.

Priyanka: I'm thinking of two short-term fixes: (A) make eviction synchronous w.r.t. shard-local read checks (i.e., bump an epoch and make read verify epoch matches) or (B) add a tiny refcount bump when handing a ptr to read path to pin during use. tradeoffs: A increases eviction latency and cross-shard handshake; B increases per-read overhead.

Jonathan: can we do lightweight epoch check without global consensus? e.g., tenant-level generation number stored in header. eviction increments generation under lock and sets ptr.gen. read verifies ptr.gen == tenant.gen. if mismatch, treat as miss.

Sam K: that matches idea in the old prefix-handshake spike but we never implemented per-tenant generation. cost: additional atomic read per cache lookup (cheap) and need to set gen when creating ptrs.

Maria G: curious about fairness: if we treat mismatch as miss, downstream will fetch from origin and repopulate. does that create thundering herd on busy tenants?

Alex C: thought about that — we can short-circuit by returning 503 for a small window or use jittered backoff on repopulation. but I prefer correctness-first: miss is fine.

Priyanka: alternative longer-term: move to lease tokens per-lookup where eviction increments token and read must CAS a slot. more complex but gives stronger invariants and measurable semantics for sharing.

Jonathan: for immediate action, I propose a two-step plan: 1) add tenant-generation check on read path (fast, low-risk). 2) run a canary for 24h in staging with multi-tenant churn sim. if stable, roll to prod.

Alex C: +1. I'll open a small PR with the gen check. pseudocode: 
```
// on allocation
ptr.gen = tenant.gen.load();
// on eviction
tenant.gen.fetch_add(1);
// on read
if (ptr.gen != tenant.gen.load()) { treat_as_miss(); }
```

Priyanka: also add a metric: "cache.eviction.mismatch_rate" per-tenant so we can see how often reads hit stale ptrs.

Sam K: I'll add the metric to the runtime telemetry.

Maria G: can you link the PR and a test plan? I'll run it against the multi-tenant perf harness.

Alex C: PR: https://github.com/redwoodinc/inference/pull/8219 (draft). test plan: 1) staging cluster with tenants A,B,C; 2) synthetic churn that evicts prefixes every 500-2000ms; 3) check mismatch_rate, correctness histograms, and tail latency.

deploy-bot: canary deploy queued for staging (canary-42).

Jonathan: one more thought — if mismatch_rate is nonzero but small, we might be OK. if it's high, we need the stronger lease token approach. Also watch for latency impact of the extra atomic on hot paths.

Priyanka: agree. timeline: Alex + Sam implement gen-check + metric today, Priyanka will run harness tomorrow, Jonathan will review. if green in 24h, ship to prod canary.

Alex C: assigning: @Priyanka run harness, @Sam K add metrics/telemetry, @Jonathan review PR, I'll iterate on PR. thanks all :thumbsup:

Maria G: thanks — and add note to eng-runtime standup agenda so oncall is aware during rollout.

Sam K: added alert: cache.eviction.mismatch_rate > 0.1% sustained -> pager.

Alex C: perfect. logging out for now, will update thread with PR updates.
